name: ANSI/IEEE impulse tachometric dynamo symbol
summary: IEEE-library impulse tacho form for a speed sensor that outputs pulses at a rate set by shaft speed.
description: The impulse form represents a speed transducer whose output is a pulse train, for example a magnetic pickup reading gear teeth or a pulse generator on the shaft. The receiving device counts pulses, so the number of pulses per revolution is the scaling factor that must accompany the symbol.

Pulse transducers may be passive magnetic pickups with amplitude rising with speed, or active sensors needing a supply. The symbol does not distinguish these, so supply wiring and input type at the receiver should be checked separately.
readingNotes: Record pulses per revolution for scaling.
Check whether the sensor is passive or needs a supply.
drawingChecklist: Use screened cable to the counter input
distinction: An impulse transducer outputs a pulse rate; a tachometric dynamo outputs an analogue voltage.
